230: 
231: ## Rust admission and source-connected state proof
232: 
233: Intent: replace the Python launcher with a Rust tool whose executing admission state machine is
234: translated by Charon/Aeneas. Development-velocity benefit is a hypothesis; no speed claim is made.
235: A Boolean conjunction over caller-supplied approvals is rejected as insufficient: only the Rust IO
236: adapter collects actual extraction/build/kernel results and identity observations. Proposal JSON
237: retains its exact schema and cannot carry approval facts. Kernel checks of the optimization theorem
238: remain external Lean checks, with their existing typed witness and cost/observation requirements.
239: 
240: Specification: zero-dependency core.rs owns opaque non-Copy Session and Permit values. start accepts
241: only a registered binding equal to the observed256-bit identity. advance consumes Session and permits
242: only the expected Extraction, Dependencies, Certificate, Revalidation event with exit0 and the same
243: binding; errors return None and release no Permit. finish consumes only the completed state and
244: rechecks the current binding. complete calls those actual bodies over four observations and a final
245: identity. SHA-256 hashes the registered source/proof/checker/worker binding; four u64 limbs are the
246: representation. No public constructor or serialized reusable permit exists. CLI checks actual JSON,
247: paths, digests and worker argv, executes bounded checks, calls complete and moves Permit into its
248: worker launch boundary. The certificate checker remains a Lean process, not a Rust decision about
249: arbitrary theorem truth.
250: 
251: Representation: Dispatch.Spec is a local workflow specification, not a new canonical algebra.
252: Dispatch.Extracted comes from a dedicated #[path] extraction unit that imports the exact tool core.
253: Dispatch.Refinement relates start/advance/finish/complete to that model and proves that a permit
254: requires every ordered successful check and unchanged identities. Constructors and joint reachable
255: success/refusal witnesses are checked. Dispatch.Audit audits all headlines under the existing closed
256: cone. Definitions, canonical pins and the foreign dirty extraction/corpus audit files remain intact.
257: 
258: Architecture boundary proposed to the independent verifier: an auxiliary tool Cargo package and
259: small extraction/Lake harness are tooling, not new canonical/runtime foundations. Lean proof files
260: remain under proof/corpus/Dispatch. IO/processes, JSON/SHA dependencies and source/cost registration
261: are tested/trusted adapters. Source mutation after checking, native bypass, codegen, OS and worker
262: sandboxing remain explicit exclusions. The production optimization registry stays empty.
